feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (score 176) and iteration 1 (score 389) show that the s-bend was limited by late reaction, not jitter. Moving the sensors to y 0.07 in iteration 2 fixed the oval (20 of 20 finishes, max_error 0.0255) and cut slalom line losses from 1.75 to 1.0, but the s-bend still lost the line in 18 of 20 trials at progress 0.64, with max_error at the 0.06 m floor and oscillation 0.30. That matches the trigger for turn authority rather than look-ahead, so narrowing wheel_track to 0.09 is a sound next test. Because the Integrator keeps kp at 2.8 and raises kd to 0.50, any s-bend result should be read as the combined effect of track width and gain. If s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1.0 and max_error drops below 0.06 on some seeds, keep wheel_track 0.09. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on the s-bend or oval, the narrower track is adding too much gain, so try 0.095 rather than further narrowing. If the oval finish rate falls below about 0.9, the gain is too high and the geometry is not the cause. The slalom at 1.0 line losses per run is near its limit for this footprint, so the 12 mm sensor size should stay unless slalom losses rise again.
requested_changes: If s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1.0 and steering_oscillation stays under about 0.35, keep wheel_track at 0.09, since iteration 2 showed the s-bend at 1.05 losses and max_error at the 0.06 floor with oscillation 0.30 on 0.10 m.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on the s-bend or oval, set wheel_track to 0.095 as an intermediate value, since the 0.09 track adds about 11% steering gain on top of iteration 2's kp 2.8, which gave oval oscillation 0.24.

If the s-bend stays at 1.0 line losses with max_error at the 0.06 floor and low oscillation, test sensor_size 0.016 with the same x positions and y 0.07 to hold the line through the s-bend, since iteration 2 showed the 12 mm footprint leaves the sensors blank at the edges and the slalom still loses 1.0 times per run.
